target_moa.text: Tafasitamab-cxix is an Fc-modified, CD19-directed cytolytic monoclonal antibody that binds CD19 on B lymphocytes and B-cell malignancies; upon binding it mediates B-cell lysis through apoptosis and immune effector mechanisms (ADCC and ADCP).

citations.quote: Tafasitamab is an Fc-modified antibody that binds to CD19 antigen expressed on the surface of pre-B and mature B lymphocytes and on several B-cell malignancies, including diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. Upon binding to CD19, tafasitamab mediates B-cell lysis through apoptosis and immune effector mechanisms, including ADCC and ADCP.

citations.quote: Tafasitamab-cxix is a humanized CD19-directed cytolytic monoclonal antibody that contains an IgG1/2 hybrid Fc-domain with 2 amino acid substitutions to modify the Fc-mediated functions of the antibody.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (≥20%) were neutropenia, fatigue, anemia, diarrhea, thrombocytopenia, cough, pyrexia, peripheral edema, respiratory tract infection, and decreased appetite. Neutropenia occurred in 51% (49% Grade 3/4) and thrombocytopenia in 31% (17% Grade 3/4). Warnings include infusion-related reactions (6% of 81 patients), myelosuppression, and infections (73% of patients developed an infection; Grade 3 or higher in 30%). Fatal adverse reactions occurred in 5% of patients.

requirement.text: 3904-1: Submit the final report and datasets from a randomized, Phase 3 clinical trial to verify the clinical benefit of tafasitamab in patients with DLBCL; patients randomized to immunotherapy and/or chemotherapy with or without tafasitamab and lenalidomide; primary endpoint progression-free survival, with secondary endpoints overall survival and objective response rate.

citations.quote: 3904-1 Submit the final report and datasets from a randomized, Phase 3 clinical trial to verify the clinical benefit of tafasitamab in patients with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. The trial should include sufficient numbers of racial and ethnic minority patients to better reflect the U.S. patient population and allow for the interpretation of the results in these patient populations. Patients should be randomized to receive immunotherapy and/or chemotherapy with or without tafasitamab and lenalidomide. The primary endpoint should be progression-free survival, with secondary endpoints that include overall survival and objective response rate.
